subject.title: [Feature]:  Missing Session Management Commands in OpenClaw

question: What first-class session lifecycle contract should OpenClaw expose for stop, kill, pause, resume, and resource-limit controls?
rationale: The requested behavior spans user-facing CLI/UI/API design, session state, child process termination, and admin authorization, which cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Define a narrow lifecycle contract first
options.body: Specify abort versus delete versus hard-kill behavior, required scopes, UI affordances, and tests before implementing additive commands.

options.title: Split into narrower existing issues
options.body: Keep this as an umbrella and route child-process kill, UI management, REST controls, and resume/fork behavior to their narrower open issues.

options.title: Defer broad lifecycle management
options.body: Document the current abort/delete/compact primitives and avoid adding new lifecycle commands until a concrete maintainer use case sponsors them.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Specify abort versus delete versus hard-kill behavior, required scopes, UI affordances, and tests before implementing additive commands.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and current-main history place this person closest to the session CLI/RPC implementation being scoped.
